title: Enterprise onboarding, health checks, and QBR playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: Canonical playbook for Enterprise customer onboarding, ongoing health checks, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). Covers phased onboarding checklist, integration guidance, support & escalation flows, known issues and workarounds, and QBR cadence/templates used by Customer Success Managers (CSMs).
content:
Purpose
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard process for enterprise onboarding, ongoing health checks, and QBRs. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Support, and Product stakeholders responsible for onboarding, operating, and growing large customers.

Scope
- Covers pre-sale handoff through 90+ day maturity.
- Includes integration guidance for common deployment patterns (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Documents standard support triage and escalation procedures and common known issues plus workarounds.
- Provides QBR cadence, KPIs, and a reusable agenda/template.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers / L2/L3 oncall
- Product & Engineering partners supporting enterprise customers

Definitions
- Go-live: customer is actively routing production traffic and using Redwood APIs in production.
- Health check: scheduled technical review of service health, cost, and quality metrics.
- QBR: business review with the customer that combines technical health and adoption/ROI discussions.

Owner & Roles
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Primary contact: Maya Chen)
- Implementation lead: Solutions Engineering (SE)
- Ongoing technical owner: Support Engineering (L2)
- Product escalation: Product Manager on call (PM-POC)

Onboarding phases and checklist
1) Pre-kickoff (sales -> CSM handoff)
   - Deliverables: signed contract, network information, contacts, initial success criteria, initial SSO/KMS requirements.
   - Actions: create account, provision customer workspace, notify Security & Legal for any special clauses.

2) Kickoff (week 0)
   - Participants: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, customer product owner, account exec (optional).
   - Agenda: goals & success metrics, timeline, roles & RACI, integration overview, data security & compliance items.
   - Deliverables: shared project plan in Asana/Jira, kickoff notes, access lists.

3) Implementation (weeks 1-4)
   - Tasks: network/firewall allowlist, API key generation and rotation policy, SSO setup (OIDC/SAML), KMS integration (if private), test prompts and workload profiling, model selection and target SLOs.
   - Integration checklist (baseline):
     - API connectivity verified (curl + SDK sample).
     - VPC peering or allowed IPs verified for Dedicated/Private customers.
     - Auth: SSO and API key setup completed.
     - Observability: customer has access to Redwood Console and cost/latency dashboards.
     - Eval set: initial prompt set and gold labels uploaded for quality monitoring.

4) Go-live (week 4-8)
   - Criteria: stable API connection, smoke tests passed, SLOs met in staging, rollback plan documented.
   - Actions: enable production credentials, set rate limits/quotas, enable billing alerts, schedule first 30/60/90 day health checks.

5) Maturity & Expansion (90+ days)
   - Ongoing: cadence of health checks (see below), QBR scheduling, model/quantization optimization recommendations, cost efficiency reviews, and adoption play facilitation.

Integration guidance (common scenarios)
- Hosted (Redwood API): Minimal network changes. Ensure TLS egress allowed and set up API key rotation. Verify streaming endpoints and webhook callbacks.
- Dedicated (reserved): Customer must provide IP allowlist and, if requested, VPC peering. Verify autoscale policies and reserved capacity thresholds.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Coordinate with Eng-Private-Deployments; verify KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and monitoring endpoints. Provide onprem agent installation checklist.

Security & Compliance checkpoints
- Confirm data residency and retention settings match contract.
- Verify KMS integration or token encryption settings when required.
- Validate audit logging and access controls for customer admins.

Support process (triage & SLAs)
- Support tiers and expected response times (enterprise customers):
  - P1 (sev:service-down): initial response <= 1 hour, patch or workaround goal <= 4 hours, continuous updates.
  - P2 (sev:degraded): initial response <= 4 hours, mitigation goal <= 24 hours.
  - P3 (feature/question/low impact): initial response <= 24 business hours.
- Triage steps (L1 -> L2 -> L3):
  1. L1 capture request in Zendesk with standard template (customer, severity, reproduction steps, timestamps, runbook link).
  2. L1 perform basic collection: logs, request IDs, sample payloads, region, model/version.
  3. L2 replicate problem in staging / use customer-provided traces.
  4. L3 / Eng involved for kernel/runtime/root-cause where necessary.

Escalation playbook (enterprise)
- Escalation matrix:
  - Level 1: CSM + L1 Support -> resolution or L2 handoff (15-60 minutes).
  - Level 2: SE + L2 Support -> technical mitigation/workaround (1-4 hours).
  - Level 3: Support Engineering Lead + Eng-oncall + Product PM -> hotfix/rollout decision (4+ hours).
- How to escalate: use internal Slack #esc-redwood-enterprise with required fields: customer-name, incident-ID, severity, impact, current mitigation. Page must be linked in ticket.
- Communication cadence: updates every 30-60 minutes for P1 until stable, then shift to hourly then daily.

Known issues & common workarounds (living list)
- Issue: High token cost due to unbatched small requests
  - Symptom: cost spikes, increased per-token latency.
  - Workaround: enable client-side request batching or use Redwood Optimize recommendations to increase batch size and reduce per-request overhead.

- Issue: Cold-start latency for large models in Dedicated pools after autoscale
  - Symptom: first request latency spike after idle period.
  - Workaround: configure warm-up requests in the application and increase minimum instances / reduce scale-down aggressiveness.

- Issue: Authentication errors after API key rotation
  - Symptom: frequent 401 from clients that cache keys.
  - Workaround: follow staged rotation flow: create new key, update clients in waves, deprecate old key after 48 hours. Document in integration checklist.

- Issue: Streaming connection resets for websocket clients behind certain proxies
  - Symptom: interrupted streams, partial responses.
  - Workaround: recommend using HTTP streaming fallback, configure proxy keepalive, or move to Redwood hosted SDK with long-lived connections.

Health checks (30/60/90 day template and cadence)
- Cadence: 30-day (technical readiness), 60-day (stability & cost), 90-day (maturity & adoption) then quarterly light checks until steady state.
- Health check attendees: CSM, SE, Support PM, customer tech lead, optionally Product PM.
- Technical agenda (30-minute template):
  1. Current usage snapshot (30s)
  2. Latency & error-rate trends (5m)
  3. Cost and token burn analysis (5m)
  4. Quality/regression check on eval set (5m)
  5. Open issues & action items (10m)
- Health metrics to track:
  - 95th / 99th percentile latency per route
  - Error rate (5xx and 4xx breakdown)
  - Tokens per successful request & cost per 1M tokens
  - Model quality metrics (BLEU/EM/ROUGE where applicable) and eval-set pass rate
  - Cache hit rate and batching efficiency

QBR playbook and template
- Frequency: Quarterly for all enterprise accounts; may increase cadence for strategic customers.
- Goals: align on business outcomes, demonstrate ROI, identify expansion opportunities, and review technical roadmap impacts.
- QBR agenda (90 minutes):
  1. Executive recap & business outcomes (10m)
  2. Adoption & usage trends (15m)
  3. Cost efficiency & optimization recommendations (15m)
  4. Reliability and incident review since last QBR (15m)
  5. Product roadmap & upcoming changes affecting the customer (15m)
  6. Action items and success plan (10m)
  7. Appendix: technical deep-dive (as needed)
- Preparation checklist for CSM:
  - Pull usage and billing export for quarter (CSV).
  - Run evals against customer prompts and summarize quality regressions.
  - Coordinate with Product on roadmap items that affect the customer.
  - Prepare 3-5 recommended optimizations (batching, quantization, model switch) with estimated $/month impact.

Templates & artifacts (links)
- QBR slide template: /templates/qbr-redwood-enterprise.pptx
- Health-check report template: /templates/health-check-report.md
- Integration checklist (runnable): /templates/integration-checklist.yaml
- Escalation Slack playbook: /templates/escalation-slack-playbook.md

Appendix: sample runbook snippets
- Collecting traces: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/requests/{request_id}/trace"
- Example SDK check (python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<key>")
  resp = client.generate(prompt="health-check", model="redwood-base-1")

- CSMs must schedule 30/60/90 health checks at go-live and attach the health-check report to the customer record.
